title: Uniform completed conormal annihilation criteria and closed base change
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring, $H\subseteq A$ an ideal, and $B$ an $H$-adically complete commutative $A$-algebra with $B/HB$ finite type over $A/H$. A finite completed polynomial presentation $B\cong\widehat{A[x_1,\ldots,x_r]}_H/J$ exists. Denote its completed conormal complex by $N_H(B/A)=(J/J^2\xrightarrow{\delta}B^{\oplus r})$, in degrees $-1,0$, where $\delta(f\bmod J^2)=(\partial f/\partial x_i\bmod J)_i$ and derivatives are continuous polynomial derivatives. Write $\mathrm{NL}_{S/R}$ for the ordinary naive cotangent complex. The following conditions are equivalent: (i) some power of $H$ annihilates both $\ker\delta$ and $\operatorname{coker}\delta$; (ii) there exists $d\geq0$ such that, for every ideal $L\subseteq A$ and every ideal $H_0\subseteq A/L$ with $V(H_0)=V(H(A/L))$, the algebra $B_L=B/LB$ is $H_0$-adically complete, has a finite completed polynomial presentation over $(A/L,H_0)$, and the image of $H^d$ annihilates both cohomology modules of its completed conormal complex, for every such presentation; (iii) for every $n\geq1$, choose a finite polynomial presentation $(A/H^n)[y_1,\ldots,y_{s_n}]\twoheadrightarrow B/H^nB$ with kernel $K_n$. There exists $e\geq0$, independent of $n$, such that $H^e$ annihilates both kernel and cokernel of $K_n/K_n^2\to(B/H^nB)^{\oplus s_n}$, $f\mapsto(\partial f/\partial y_j)_j$, for every $n$. Condition (i) is independent of the chosen finite completed polynomial presentation. The exponents in (i), (ii), and (iii) need not be equal. The ring, completion, polynomial, finite-type, cotangent and scheme notions used here, when present, are those of [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra, def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The completed conormal differential is the construction of [def-per-completed-polynomial-conormal].

source.place: Tag 0AJU (lemma-equivalent-with-artin), conditions (3),(4), with Tag 0AK2 (lemma-zero-after-modding-out) and remark-take-bar for the uniform closed-base-change formulation. Tag 0GAE (lemma-NL-up-to-homotopy) gives independence of presentation. The uniform exponent in (ii) is obtained from one power acting as zero on the original complex, before varying L; it is not an assertion that independently chosen base-change exponents are bounded.

proof.text: Apply the completed-cotangent transitivity node with $C=B$ and the identity map. Its hypotheses are exactly completeness and finite type modulo $H$ for both copies of $B$. It supplies a finite completed polynomial presentation, Noetherianity of $B$, and homotopy independence of the resulting complexes. Fix $P=\widehat{A[x_1,\ldots,x_r]}_H$, $J=\ker(P\to B)$, $M=J/J^2$, $F=B^{\oplus r}$ and $\delta:M\to F$. Homotopy inverse chain maps induce inverse maps on kernels and cokernels: on a cycle the difference from the identity is a boundary, and boundaries are quotiented out. Thus condition (i), with its chosen exponent, is independent of presentation.

Assume (i), with exponent $c$. For $a\in H^c$, lift each $a e_j\in F$ through $\delta$ using $a\operatorname{coker}\delta=0$, and let $\alpha:F\to M$ send $e_j$ to that lift. Then $\delta\alpha=a\operatorname{id}_F$. Since $\alpha\delta(m)-am\in\ker\delta$ and $a\ker\delta=0$, the map $h=a\alpha$ satisfies $\delta h=a^2\operatorname{id}_F$ and $h\delta=a^2\operatorname{id}_M$. This basis calculation also works when $r=0$.

source.place: Tag 0AJU, (3) implies (2); explicit two-term homotopy calculation replacing the derived-category argument.

proof.text: Fix $L\subseteq A$ and put $A_0=A/L$, $B_0=B/LB$, $R=A[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$ and $R_0=A_0[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$. The finite-type Noetherian theorem gives Noetherianity of $R$ and $A_0$. Apply the finite-module completion comparison to the cyclic $B$-module $B_0$: since $B$ is $H$-complete, its canonical completion map is bijective, so $B_0$ is $H$-complete. Apply that comparison also to the cyclic $R$-module $R/LR$. It gives $\widehat{R_0}_H\cong P\otimes_R(R/LR)\cong P/LP$. The tensor-quotient maps are $p\otimes\bar f\mapsto pf\bmod LP$ and $\bar p\mapsto p\otimes1$; the completion comparison sends them to their coordinate reductions, so this is an algebra isomorphism, not just a module isomorphism.

Let $H_0\subseteq A_0$ satisfy the required equality of zero loci and put $T=HA_0$. Equality of radicals follows from the zero-locus node. Since $A_0$ is Noetherian, the radical-power lemma gives $T^u\subseteq H_0$ and $H_0^v\subseteq T$ for some $u,v\geq1$. The change-of-ideal theorem applied to $B_0$ and $R_0$ makes $B_0$ $H_0$-complete and identifies $P/LP$ with $P_0=\widehat{R_0}_{H_0}$. The quotient map $\pi:P\twoheadrightarrow P_0$ has kernel $LP$. With $J_0=\pi(J)$, it gives $B_0=P_0/J_0$. Also $B_0/H_0B_0$ is finite type over $A_0/H_0$: the completion-mod-power theorem identifies $P_0/H_0P_0$ with $(A_0/H_0)[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$, which surjects onto that quotient.

Set $M_0=J_0/J_0^2$, $F_0=B_0^{\oplus r}$ and let $q:M\twoheadrightarrow M_0$ and $\rho:F\twoheadrightarrow F_0$ be reduction. The first map is surjective since $\pi(J)=J_0$, and is well defined since $\pi(J^2)=J_0^2$. Derivatives on $P$ are computed on compatible polynomial reductions. Coefficient reduction and cofinal reindexing commute with these derivatives; hence $\delta_0q=\rho\delta$. For the map $h$ in Step 2, $qh$ kills $LF$ and induces $h_0:F_0\to M_0$. Now $\delta_0h_0\rho=\rho\delta h=a^2\rho$ and $h_0\delta_0q=qh\delta=a^2q$. Surjectivity gives $\delta_0h_0=\bar a^2\operatorname{id}$ and $h_0\delta_0=\bar a^2\operatorname{id}$. Thus $\bar a^2$ kills both cohomology modules, for every $a\in H^c$. The derivative construction and the homotopy equations alone justify this step; tensor exactness on kernels is not asserted.

source.place: Tag 0GAG (lemma-NL-base-change) and Tag 0AK2 (lemma-zero-after-modding-out), explicit closed-quotient calculation.

proof.text: Choose ideal generators $b_1,\ldots,b_t$ of $H^c$ in the Noetherian ring $A$. Every product of $t+1$ of these generators repeats a factor, so $H^{c(t+1)}=(H^c)^{t+1}\subseteq(b_1^2,\ldots,b_t^2)$. For $t=0$ this inclusion still holds because $H^c=0$. Step 5 therefore shows that the image of $H^d$, $d=c(t+1)$, kills both cohomology modules for the constructed presentation of every $B_0$, independently of $L,H_0$. The completed-cotangent node, applied over $A_0$ with $C=B_0$, applies by Step 4 and gives homotopy independence for every other finite completed presentation. The induced cohomology isomorphisms are $B_0$-linear, so the same $H^d$ kills them all. This proves (ii). Taking $L=0,H_0=H$ in (ii) proves (i).

source.place: Tag 0AJU, uniform ideal-power bound; Tag 0GAE for independence of presentation.

proof.text: Condition (ii) implies (iii) by $L=H^n$ and $H_0=0\subseteq A/H^n$. Indeed $H(A/H^n)$ is nilpotent, so its zero locus is the entire spectrum, equal to $V(0)$. Completion with respect to zero is the ring itself: the defining inverse system is constant. Consequently every finite polynomial presentation in (iii) is a completed polynomial presentation over $(A/H^n,0)$. The single exponent $d$ in (ii) therefore works for all $n$, with every prescribed choice of presentation.

source.place: Tag 0AJU, (3) implies (4), via the uniform closed-base-change conclusion.

proof.text: For the converse assume (iii), with exponent $e$. The completion-mod-power theorem identifies $P/H^nP$ with $(A/H^n)[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$. Thus the fixed presentation induces presentations with kernels $J_n=(J+H^nP)/H^nP$. The ordinary polynomial-presentation homotopy theorem and the polynomial differential basis identify the kernels and cokernels of these conormal differentials with those for the presentations chosen in (iii). Hence $H^e$ kills the kernel and cokernel of every $\delta_n:J_n/J_n^2\to(B/H^nB)^{\oplus r}$ for these induced presentations. No compatibility between the presentations chosen in (iii) is required.

source.place: Tag 0AJS (lemma-NL-is-limit), first presentation calculation; algebra.tex Tags 05GG, 00S1, 00RX.

proof.text: The ring $R=A[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$ is Noetherian by finite-type permanence, and $P=\widehat R_H$ is Noetherian by the completion theorem. Hence $J$ is finitely generated. Its generating classes generate $M=J/J^2$ over $B$: changing a coefficient by an element of $J$ changes its product with a generator by an element of $J^2$. Also $C=\operatorname{coker}\delta$ is finite over $B$, as a quotient of $F$. Since $B$ is Noetherian and $H$-complete, the finite-module completion comparison gives bijective canonical completion maps for $M$ and $C$. In particular $\bigcap_{k\geq1}H^kM=0$ and $\bigcap_{k\geq1}H^kC=0$, because an element in either intersection has every completion coordinate zero.

For $a\in H^e$ and $w\in F$, the image of $aw$ lies in $\operatorname{im}\delta_n$ for every $n$. Lift a representative of that preimage from $J_n$ to $J$; its derivative differs from $aw$ by an element of $H^nF$. Thus $aw\in\operatorname{im}\delta+H^nF$, so $a[w]\in H^nC$ for every $n$. The separatedness in Step 9 gives $a[w]=0$. This proves $H^e\operatorname{coker}\delta=0$.

Apply Artin-Rees in the Noetherian ring $P$ to the ideal $HP$, the finite module $P$ and submodule $J$. It gives $k\geq0$ with $J\cap H^nP\subseteq H^{n-k}J$ for $n\geq k$. For $x=[f]\in\ker\delta$ and $a\in H^e$, its image in $J_n/J_n^2$ belongs to $\ker\delta_n$ and is killed by $a$. The kernel of $J\to J_n/J_n^2$ is $J^2+(J\cap H^nP)$: the inverse image of $J_n^2$ is $J^2+H^nP$, and intersecting with $J$ gives the formula. Therefore $af\in J^2+(J\cap H^nP)\subseteq J^2+H^{n-k}J$ for every $n\geq\max(1,k)$. Passing to $M$ shows $ax\in H^{n-k}M$ for arbitrarily large $n$. Step 9 implies $ax=0$. This proves $H^e\ker\delta=0$, hence (i), and completes all equivalences. The argument does not identify $J_n/J_n^2$ with $M/H^nM$; Artin-Rees supplies precisely the needed error bound.
